title: CodeRL: Mastering Code Generation through Pretrained Models and Deep Reinforcement Learning
data_curation: Training/eval data centers on two Python benchmarks. APPS has 10,000 coding problems (50-50 train/test split) with ~23.2 reference programs and ~21.2 unit tests per problem, split into Introductory (3639), Interview (5000), and Competition (1361) difficulties. MBPP is smaller/simpler: 974 instances (374/90/500 train/val/test), one solution plus 3 assert-style unit tests each, used for zero-shot transfer. For pretraining, the authors extend CodeT5 by enlarging the Python corpus with the permissively-licensed Github Code Python dataset (GCPY), yielding 10.5B tokens (10x larger than CodeSearchNet's CSN), and by adding a next-token-prediction (NTP) objective alongside masked span prediction (MSP). Synthetic code samples drawn from the actor LM (both passing and failing) are reused to train the critic and the program-repair model, with ground-truth programs labeled PassedTest.
curriculum: Stage order is: (1) two-stage pretraining of CodeT5-large (770M) — MSP on CSN for 150 epochs then GCPY for 10 epochs, followed by NTP for 10 epochs; (2) warm-start finetuning with cross-entropy Lce only for up to 10 epochs (imitation learning) to avoid the unstable actor-critic feedback loop; (3) critic training on synthetic samples while the actor is frozen; (4) RL finetuning combining Lce and Lrl with equal weights. Rationale: Lrl alone causes vanishing gradients, while Lce alone overfits after ~epoch 10, so the mixed objective stabilizes and prevents overfitting. At inference, an optional Critic Sampling loop (max one repair round then one refine round) re-runs generation conditioned on test outcomes. The pipeline is model-agnostic and was also applied to GPT-Neo and GPT-J actors.
method: CodeRL casts program synthesis as an RL problem with an actor-critic scheme. The pretrained LM is the actor/policy; a smaller Transformer critic is trained as a 4-class error predictor (CompileError, RuntimeError, FailedTest, PassedTest). Returns from unit tests are heuristic: -1.0 compile error, -0.6 runtime error, -0.3 failed test, +1.0 all pass. To cut gradient variance the return is made relative to a greedy-decoding baseline, and dense token-level feedback q_hat_phi(w_t^s) comes from the critic's per-token hidden states, giving the policy-gradient update in Eq. (10). The inference-time Critic Sampling (CS) dual strategy: program refining uses critic-scored sub-sequences of example-test-passing programs as seeds to resample; program repairing sends the top-M critic-selected failed programs plus compiler error types/messages to a seq2seq repair model trained on synthetic buggy/correct pairs. CS is limited to one repair and one refine round, with nucleus sampling at batch N=200.
eval_metrics: Primary metrics are pass@k (k=1,5,1000) and n@k (filtered subset of n from k candidates via example-test filtering), plus pass@80 and pass@1000 for MBPP; CodeXGLUE tasks use BLEU-4, CodeBLEU, and EM. Benchmarks: APPS, MBPP (zero-shot and finetuned), and CodeXGLUE. Headline APPS results for CodeRL+CodeT5-770M: 2.69% pass@1, 6.81% pass@5, 20.98% pass@1000 (all new SOTA), and 8.48% 1@k, 12.62% 5@k — matching AlphaCode-1B with k=50000 using only k=1000. Zero-shot MBPP: 63.0% pass@80 (new SOTA over GPT-137B's 61.4%) and 81.8% pass@1000. Ablations confirm relative+critic returns (Model D) and combined Lce+Lrl are best; CS adds gains especially at pass@1000; critic reaches >75% error-prediction accuracy.
key_results: CodeRL+CodeT5-770M sets APPS SOTA at 2.69% pass@1, 6.81% pass@5, 20.98% pass@1000, and 8.48% 1@k / 12.62% 5@k. Zero-shot on MBPP it reaches 63.0% pass@80 and 81.8% pass@1000, beating GPT-137B (61.4%) with a far smaller model.
evolution_note: CodeRL extends the REINFORCE/actor-critic line for sequence generation (Ranzato 2016, Bahdanau 2016) and CodeT5 pretraining into code, reacting to the neglect of unit-test signals and the limits of NTP-only SFT. In 2022 it anticipated the later trend of execution-feedback and reward-model-driven post-training for code, showing that test outcomes and critic scores can shape both training and test-time decoding.
